It is not an acquired disorder and is not related to anticardiolipin antibodies. The presence of Factor V Leiden does not prolong the partial thromboplastin time (PTT), which remains normal in most cases. Together with the prothrombin mutation, Factor V Leiden constitutes the most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition in the population. Therefore, the correct statement is option 'opd'.
analysis: Factor V Leiden is a genetic mutation that leads to resistance to activated protein C, which increases the risk of thrombosis. It is not an acquired disorder and is not associated with anticardiolipin antibodies. The presence of Factor V Leiden does not prolong the partial thromboplastin time (PTT), which typically remains normal. The most significant point is that Factor V Leiden, along with the prothrombin mutation, is indeed the most common genetic predisposition to thrombosis in the population.
